extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, press release writers, marketers, and communications teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting effective calls-to-action (CTAs) in press releases to drive traffic, engagement, and conversions while preserving newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a clear, compelling CTA relevant to your overall message
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release campaigns, should also include a clear, compelling CTA relevant to your overall message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can help maximize engagement and, most importantly, conversions. Make sure the CTA fits the announcement and overall campaign goal rather than being an unrelated promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct readers to a next step to stay engaged with your brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs your readers to take the next step and stay engaged with your brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desired actions include visiting your website, filling out a form, or contacting your sales team. The CTA should make the next action explicit and attainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make CTAs trackable to gauge distribution effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives you a gauge on the effectiveness of your press release distribution by tracking the number of clicks and conversions of your CTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use trackable links, UTM parameters, or gated content to measure clicks and conversions and evaluate how well the release drove the intended outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the CTA at the end of the main body
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release CTA is typically placed at the end of the main body of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This placement ensures the reader understands the topic and is more informed to take the desired action. Avoid placing a CTA before the reader has necessary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be direct about the action you want the reader to take
rubrics_metrics.description: Be direct and share the action you want the reader to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity causes friction, which makes a reader less likely to engage. Use unambiguous phrasing so there is no question what the user should do next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why the reader should take the action (answer 'what's in it for me?')
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why someone would want to take the action. Create your call-to-action from your audience’s perspective and answer the question, what's in it for me?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include benefit-focused copy or a short sentence that tells the reader what they will gain or learn by clicking or signing up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use action-oriented language
rubrics_metrics.description: When drafting your copy, use action-oriented language such as “Subscribe,” “Buy Now,” “Register,” and “Download.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer verbs that prompt immediate action. Avoid passive or vague phrasing that doesn't compel the user to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance CTA tone with newsworthiness (avoid sounding overtly promotional)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the challenges of blending a call to action with your “news” is that CTAs tend to sound a bit sales-y and promotional. That goes directly against the general function of a press release, which is to announce something newsworthy. However, you can find a good balance with a “learn more” type of call to action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use softer CTAs (e.g., “Learn more”) that invite further information rather than hard sells. Provide something specific to learn about and avoid aggressive promotional language that undermines the release’s credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Learn More' CTAs to drive traffic to additional content
rubrics_metrics.description: With this type of CTA, you’ll want to provide readers with something specific that they can learn more about. You may also want to create an additional piece of content for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: “Learn more about how KEY FINDINGS impact you, visit LINK” or “Learn more about how KEY FINDINGS impact you, get the REPORT here.” This type of CTA drives traffic to a specific webpage and can be paired with gated content to capture leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use limited-time/scarcity CTAs when appropriate to create urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Scarcity is an effective motivator. If you’re announcing a product, promotion, or new service with a press release, you might consider creating a sense of urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make offers time-bound or limited in quantity, but balance urgency with the news angle so the release still reads as announcement rather than pure promotion. Example CTAs: “Click here to preorder PRODUCT/SERVICE”, “Sign up for product updates LINK”, “View more information on the product LINK”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple invitation CTAs to grow community and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: A third option for your CTA is to simply invite your readers to engage and connect. This is a good way to grow your community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite readers to sign up for newsletters, demos, consultations, or contact forms and include one or two sentences sharing the benefits. Examples: “Sign up for a one hour consultation and discover how we can help you…LINK”, “Get weekly tips on how to….LINK”, “Become a part of our community. Get the inside scoop on sales, products, and tips before anyone else LINK.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gated content/email capture strategically to build lists
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also require an email address to deliver the report to your reader and subsequently build a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering a report or downloadable asset via a press-release CTA, consider gating the asset to collect email addresses for follow-up and list-building; ensure this aligns with privacy/consent requirements and the expectations set in the release.
